title: Teaching LLMs to Speak Spotify — Yves Raimond & Jacqueline Wood, Spotify
talk_summary: Spotify describes NEO, a four-stage training recipe that teaches open-weight LLMs to emit 'semantic ID' tokens for catalog items, enabling grounded, language-steerable recommendation with low-latency tool-free inference. They also detail how they ground LLM judges in real behavioral/profile data to make automated evaluation align with human preferences.

takeaways.technique: Ground LLM judges in real user/behavioral context
takeaways.what_they_do: They feed textual user profiles summarizing listening history, and past interactions on similar queries, into the LLM judge so its verdicts track human preference rather than judging in a vacuum.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to invest in grounding your LLM judges in meaningful data so that they can be reliable evaluators that align with human preferences
takeaways.numbers: 75% judge-human alignment with profiles; +5% overall and +91% on ambiguous queries from behavioral grounding; 0.87 agreement on system rankings

takeaways.technique: Scale human-ranked eval sets with grounded LLM judges
takeaways.what_they_do: They build Cranfield-style pools from multiple candidate sources, then replace the expensive human ranking stage with a heavily grounded LLM judge once it aligns with human system rankings.
They compared beam search, constrained decoding, and top-p sampling for structured token output, choosing beam search despite latency because sampling hurt accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: top P sampling pretty significantly hurts our accuracy. So although beam search is a little more latency intensive, we decided that trade-off worked for us
takeaways.numbers: 98% valid semantic IDs even without constrained decoding

takeaways.technique: Freeze backbone while learning new tokens to avoid forgetting
takeaways.what_they_do: In domain grounding they freeze the LLM and train only new embeddings, preserving core language ability; continuous pre-training degraded world knowledge to near zero.
takeaways.numbers: continuous pre-training drove natural-language/world-knowledge ability to essentially zero

takeaways.technique: Multitask training beats single-task, helps cold start
takeaways.what_they_do: One model trained on many tasks matched or beat single-task models, with cross-learning helping new/cold-start content types.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the multitask model can match or actually beat the single task performance indicating that there is some positive cross-learning happening across the tasks
takeaways.numbers: multitask matched/beat single-task across tasks; notable gains on cold-start audiobooks
